claim.claim-text: in response to receiving a first user input for searching the wireless ultrasound probe, control the first communicator to output a pairing signal, in response to the first communicator being paired with the wireless ultrasound probe and receiving identification (ID) information of the paired wireless ultrasound probe, control the display to display the ID information of the paired wireless ultrasound probe, and in response to receiving a second user input for activating the paired wireless ultrasound probe, control the first communicator or the second communicator to transmit an activation signal to the paired wireless ultrasound probe and control the second communicator to receive the ultrasound image data from the paired wireless ultrasound probe.
2. The electronic device of claim 1, wherein the first communicator is Bluetooth communication module, and the second communicator is Wi-Fi Direct communication module.

3. The electronic device of claim 2, wherein the controller is further configured to, in response to receiving battery charging information of the paired wireless ultrasound probe through the first communicator, control the display to display the battery charging information of the paired wireless ultrasound probe.

4. The electronic device of claim 2, wherein the controller is configured to control the display to display an ultrasound image corresponding to the ultrasound image data received from the paired wireless ultrasound probe through the second communicator.

5. The electronic device of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to, in response to receiving the second user input, control the first communicator or the second communicator to transmit a beam forming control signal for controlling a beam former of the paired wireless ultrasound probe to the paired wireless ultrasound probe.

6. The electronic device of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to, in response to receiving a third user input for setting a time gain compensation value, control the first communicator or the second communicator to transmit a control signal for setting the time gain compensation value of the paired wireless ultrasound probe.

7. The electronic device of claim 4, wherein the controller is further configured to, in response to receiving a third user input for freezing the ultrasound image, control the display to pause the ultrasound image being displayed on the display.

8. The electronic device of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to, in response to receiving the ID information of the paired wireless ultrasound probe through the first communicator, control the display to display a thumbnail image representing a shape of the paired wireless ultrasound probe.

9. The electronic device of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to, in response to receiving an activation completion signal from the paired wireless ultrasound probe, control the display to display a visual indicator indicating that the paired wireless ultrasound probe is being activated.

10. The electronic device of claim 1, further comprising a speaker, wherein the controller is further configured to, in response to the first communicator being paired with the wireless ultrasound probe, control the speaker to output a preset sound.
11. A non-transitory computer-readable medium storing computer-executable instructions when executed by at least one processor of an electronic device, cause the electronic device to perform:

12. The non-transitory computer-readable medium according to claim 11, wherein the first communicator is Bluetooth communication module, and the second communicator is Wi-Fi Direct communication module.

13. The non-transitory computer-readable medium according to claim 11, wherein when executed by the at least one processor of the electronic device, the instructions cause the electronic device to further perform: in response to receiving battery charging information of the paired wireless ultrasound probe through the first communicator, controlling the display to display the battery charging information of the paired wireless ultrasound probe.

14. The non-transitory computer-readable medium according to claim 11, wherein when executed by the at least one processor of the electronic device, the instructions cause the electronic device to further perform: controlling the display to display an ultrasound image corresponding to the ultrasound image data received from the paired wireless ultrasound probe through the second communicator.

15. The non-transitory computer-readable medium according to claim 11, wherein when executed by the at least one processor of the electronic device, the instructions cause the electronic device to further perform: in response to receiving the second user input, controlling the first communicator or the second communicator to transmit a beam forming control signal for controlling a beam former of the paired wireless ultrasound probe to the paired wireless ultrasound probe.
